page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a KVM-hypervised virtual server featuring 20 shared vCPUs mapped to 20 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 64 GB of system memory, yielding 3.2 GB of RAM per core. This configuration does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it does provide one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%, reflecting the shared nature of the CPU allocation. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and small-model LLM inference tasks show strong performance, placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth and database operations consistently rank in the middle 50%.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage, this server offers a resource-dense profile suited for workloads that can tolerate shared-core variability. It is appropriate for multi-threaded processing, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference tasks. It is less suitable for single-threaded, high-performance computing or database workloads requiring dedicated, non-shared CPU resources.
description: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-64GB is a KVM-based virtual server configured with 20 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 64 GB of system memory (3.2 GB per core) and does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench scores placing in the middle 50%, while single-core performance is limited, ranking in the bottom 10% due to the shared CPU allocation. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and small-model LLM inference demonstrate strong performance in the top 25%. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for resource-dense, multi-threaded workloads such as static web serving, lightweight text processing, and parallelized data decompression where dedicated CPU performance is not a strict requirement.
